done.why: I died a second time setting myself on fire in the balloon basket. My treasures went off to the Wizard's cabinet behind the lizard door and my newspaper was ash, so I was back in the barrow with a lamp and nothing else. Doing the whole trek again through the spinning carousel room, which sends you somewhere random, was more than I had patience for.

about: You're shut inside a barrow under the Great Underground Empire, and you go south across a ravine after a petty, cackling Wizard who has hoarded the Empire's lost treasures. There's a formal garden with a unicorn that won't give up its key, a hungry lizard head set into a door, a riddle door, a spinning carousel room, a dragon you trick into melting a glacier, and a hot-air balloon at the bottom of a volcano. It's the old Zork II with a gentler voice. When it won't let you do something, it often tells you why, and sometimes it hints at what would work.

moments.note: Hitting the lantern with the sword got 'I've known strange people, but fighting a lamp?' It's a fun reply, even if it sounds like a stock line.
Knocking on the barrow door: nobody answers, 'which... is a relief.'
The Wizard showed up, more or less read me the map with a look, then cast Feeble and I dropped the lamp.
Throwing the sword into the chasm just got a flat 'You can't', with no reason given.
Typing a plain 'jump' on the bridge killed me with a swan-dive, and I woke up in a sphere of red mist.
A huge face in the black mist sent me back to life, and it wants a favour later.
The unicorn's ribbon is 'tied for somebody in particular', and it holds its head out of reach until I give up. A refusal that comes with a story.
My sword from before I died was sitting in the gazebo.
'strike a match' was read as attacking the matchbook.
I fed the place mat to the lizard. It ate it anyway, stayed exactly as hungry, and won't give it back.
Saying 'a well, obviously' only got a hollow laugh. It wanted 'answer well' exactly.
Typing 'up' in the carousel got an explanation of why there's no up, plus a hint about machinery under the floor.
Examining the bucket pointed me toward ford water and the teapot. It was a nice, fair nudge.
Pouring water on the dragon wasted the teapot water I'd walked all that way to get.
The dragon gave up following me after one room. Turns out you have to keep provoking it in every room.
The dragon saw its reflection in the glacier, breathed fire, melted the ice, swallowed the flood and exploded. A great payoff.
Burning the newspaper while holding it killed me, and every treasure got shipped off behind the lizard door.
The carousel kept throwing me to Topiary, Cobwebby Corridor or the Menhir Room when I wanted the riddle room. It ate dozens of turns.

wished: To wear the pearl necklace, or lick a lantern, or talk the lamp into telling me about its last adventure
To prune the topiary dragon with my sword, or break off a stalactite
To throw the sword into the ravine just to see what happens
For the riddle door to take 'a well, obviously' as an answer
Some way to stand still in the carousel and wait for the passage I wanted
To argue with the face in the black mist, or refuse to go back
To tie the black string to something, anything

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you
lines.why: The Wizard gives away the whole map while sneering at me, and that's very much his character.

lines.line: It will wait for her. You need not.
lines.why: A lovely, firm 'no' that tells me to stop trying.

lines.line: That was not what it wanted; it ate it because it was there, and it will not be giving it back.
lines.why: It's funny, and it also tells me what the lizard actually wants.

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: A wink at the lantern from the first game, and it got me poking at it.

lines.line: There is a muffled explosion and the dragon, a puzzled expression on his face, dies.
lines.why: The best payoff I got all game.

lines.line: The newspaper catches fire. Unfortunately, you were holding it at the time.
lines.why: Deadpan and deserved, but it ended my run.

lines.line: Your reflection in the glass is at a different angle from you.
lines.why: An eerie little detail that made the odd-angled room memorable.

fun.why: The dragon set piece and the lizard eating my place mat were great fun. The carousel and two careless deaths drained a lot of it away.

engagement.why: The hints in the descriptions (bucket, lizard, glacier) kept pulling me forward. The random carousel trips and losing everything when I died wore my patience down.

difficulty.why: The puzzles were fair and hinted. But the parser was picky about wording (riddle, 'strike a match'), the carousel made getting anywhere a gamble, and one slip with fire cost me every treasure I had.

interestingness.why: The Wizard, the face in the mist and the unicorn waiting for 'her' all feel like there's a bigger story going on. Even the refusals hinted at what would work.

prose.why: Dry and witty, especially in the new descriptions of the lantern, the lizard, the bucket and the unicorn. The stock replies ('You can't see any such thing') stuck out next to them.
